headline: A fund manager told The Australian that the failed share market debut of the AI data centre company Firmus holds lessons for investors in the AI boom.
score_reason: Headline only and the collapse happened about 9 Oct 2026, before the 14 Oct window; the pool score of 5 is lowered by 1.
importance_line: Investors in AI listings and data centre companies are most affected, along with the Australian market; what the fund manager's lessons are is not confirmed.
summary: The Australian reports that a fund manager says the failed float of Firmus, an Australian AI data centre company, carries key lessons for investors in the AI boom.
notes: The Australian returned HTTP 403 (paywall); Stockhead and Switzer Daily were also blocked. Context from Oz Arab Media, relaying The Guardian: the planned Firmus listing collapsed 'last Friday' (9 Oct 2026), had been called the biggest ASX listing since Telstra, and co-founder Oliver Curtis blamed Australian disbelief of entrepreneurs. Not included in the summary because it is second-hand. Headline only; the fund manager is not named. Score lowered from 5 to 4 (older event, unverified).
